item.title: Sydney man charged with car bomb plot and downloading Islamic State group material
item.description:
Sydney man charged with car bomb plot and downloading Islamic State group material
Australian police have arrested a man in the greater Sydney area on charges of researching how to build a car bomb and downloading violent material inspired by the Islamic State groupByROD MCGUIRK Associated PressNovember 20, 2026, 12:29 AM
Share
MELBOURNE, Australia -- Australian police on Friday arrested a man in the greater Sydney area on charges of researching how to build a car bomb and downloading violent material inspired by the Islamic State group.
Police stressed they found no evidence of a link to the upcoming first anniversary of an IS-inspired attack at Sydney’s Bondi Beach. Two gunmen opened fire on a Dec. 14 Hanukkah celebration, leaving 15 people dead and 40 wounded.
Nowroz Rayed Amin, 35, from Ingleburn on Sydney’s southwestern outskirts, was charged with collecting documents likely to facilitate terrorist acts and possessing violent extremist material obtained online, Australian Federal Police Deputy Commissioner Hilda Sirec said.
“It will be alleged in court that the man was researching how to build a vehicle-borne, improvised explosive device, which we allege, for use in a potential terrorist act,” Sirec told reporters.
Amin appeared in the Campbelltown Local Court later Friday on the two charges, which carry a potential combined maximum penalty of 20 years in prison.
Amin did not enter pleas or apply for release on bail. He was remanded in custody to appear in court on Thursday next week, court documents show.
Investigators decided to make the arrest Friday because there was sufficient evidence and not because of any imminent threat to the community, according to Sirec, who said police suspected he had acted alone.

item.title: El Salvador President Nayib Bukele seeks third term while attacking gangs in Haiti
item.description:
El Salvador President Nayib Bukele seeks third term while attacking gangs in Haiti
El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele has officially launched his bid for reelection in the February electionsByYOLANDA MAGAÑA Associated Press and MEGAN JANETSKY Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 10:15 PM
Share
SAN SALVADOR -- SAN SALVADOR (AP) — El Salvador President Nayib Bukele on Thursday night officially launched his candidacy for a third term in office after years of paving the way to stay in power indefinitely.
With virtually no political opposition, the highly popular leader is positioned to coast easily into a third term in office in the February elections. Recent polls put his approval ratings around 90%, largely due to his war on the country’s gangs, which fueled accusations of mass human rights abuses but sharply reduced violence.
The firebrand populist submitted his presidential candidate paperwork to the country’s Supreme Electoral Tribunal. His New Ideas party, which holds a supermajority in the country’s congress, cleared the way for him to be the party’s candidate in July and remain in power.
Crowds of supporters carrying “Bukele 2027” signs cheered his arrival in a fleet of police cars at the electoral tribunal building, where candidates for 60 congressional seats and 44 municipal council seats also submitted documentation ahead of the Thursday night deadline.
The reelection bid comes as Bukele has taken his crime offensive to Haiti. He deployed around 2,500 troops to fight gangs after the disappearance of four Salvadoran aviation technicians in an October gang attack.
Critics have described the offensive as a way to offset international scrutiny, rally domestic support ahead of elections and solidify Bukele’s long-term political project. But Bukele, a former communications strategist, often seems to enjoy political spectacles.

item.title: European troops from 11 countries drill in Poland for a potential postwar Ukraine mission
item.description:
European troops from 11 countries drill in Poland for a potential postwar Ukraine mission
Thousands of European troops are taking part in a major military exercise in southeastern PolandByCLAUDIA CIOBANU Associated Press and RAFAL NIEDZIELSKI Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 5:59 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
NOWA DEBA, Poland -- Thousands of European troops are taking part in an unprecedented military exercise in southeastern Poland to prepare for a potential postwar mission in Ukraine aimed at helping to stabilize the country and rebuild its military once the war ends.
Led by France and the U.K., the multinational force is a non-NATO military initiative of the so-called Coalition of the Willing, a wider political group of 37 nations supporting Ukraine.
The two-week exercise that began on Nov. 9 is for the first time checking this coalition's ability to deploy in Ukraine once the war ends. It is aimed both at testing deployment plans and sending a message to Russia and the Trump administration that European countries are stepping up militarily.
The exercise took place as leaders from Ukraine and nearly 40 other delegations met in Berlin to underline their support for Kyiv and explore Ukraine’s postwar security arrangements. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wants to ensure that Russia doesn’t invade again, while Moscow wants to keep the NATO military alliance away from its borders.
U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday he believes Russia is “comfortable” with NATO-like security guarantees for postwar Ukraine. Kushner and fellow U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff were in Berlin to reassure European leaders about U.S. President Donald Trump’s discussions on ending the nearly 5-year-old war at his historic trilateral talks with Russian leader Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Trump called into the Berlin talks following his meeting with Putin, according to Kushner.

item.title: Brazil's Lula moves to protect Chief Raoni’s birthplace in the Amazon rainforest
item.description:
Brazil's Lula moves to protect Chief Raoni’s birthplace in the Amazon rainforest
The Brazilian government has advanced legal protection for the territory of Raoni Metuktire, a prominent Indigenous leader in the AmazonByGABRIELA SÁ PESSOA Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 3:51 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
SAO PAULO -- The Brazilian government Thursday advanced legal protection for the territory of Raoni Metuktire, the Amazon’s most internationally recognized Indigenous leader, during a visit by Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to the Indigenous territory in the Brazilian rainforest.
The Justice Ministry’s order formally recognized the Mebengokre-Kayapo and Yudja-Juruna peoples’ permanent possession of the Kapot Nhinore Indigenous Territory, where chief Raoni was born.
Lula said the government still faces legal hurdles to complete the demarcation because about 200 rural properties overlap the territory.
“But we’re going to work very hard to resolve this once and for all,” he said at a public event in the Indigenous territory, streamed on the government’s official YouTube channel.
The size of the land — 362,000 hectares (895,000 acres) for 60 people — has been a sticking point in land recognition discussions.
“It doesn’t matter if it’s one person. We cannot decide whether to recognize Indigenous land based on how much land people will have," Lula said. "We must never forget that Raoni’s ancestors were here before there were any Brazilians. We are simply restoring the rights and dignity you should never have lost.”
The Kapot Nhinore territory lies along the Xingu River, a major Amazon tributary, on the border between Para and Mato Grosso states. Raoni has fought for decades for the territory’s permanent protection, but the Brazilian government only formally defined its boundaries in 2023, as part of an administrative process that began in 2004.

item.title: Dozens of inmates in Romania step onto the stage for the 15th edition of a prison theater festival
item.description:
Dozens of inmates in Romania step onto the stage for the 15th edition of a prison theater festival
A drama festival in Romania gives dozens of prison inmates a brief respite from life behind bars as they perform on stage at a renowned theater in the capitalBySTEPHEN MCGRATH Associated Press and NICOLAE DUMITRACHE Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 1:35 PM
BUCHAREST, Romania -- A drama festival in Romania gave dozens of prison inmates a brief respite this week from life behind bars as they stepped into the limelight, performing on stage at a renowned theater in the capital.
This year’s 15th edition of the “Dana Cenusa — Unshackling through Culture” Multiart Festival, organized by the National Administration of Penitentiaries at the Nottara Theatre in Bucharest, brought together 59 inmates from seven different prisons across the country.
Launched in 2009, the prison theater festival offers inmates a route toward integration and hopes to combat stereotypes by giving theatergoers an opportunity “to discover the human being beyond their legal status.”
Madalina Iosif, spokesperson for the prison administration, told The Associated Press that social reintegration is not just about prisoners serving custodial sentences but also engaging inmates in educational and social activities to prepare them "for a fresh start.”
The performances — collaborations between 12 theater professionals — showed off a range of themes, from an adaptation of Samuel Beckett’s “Waiting for Godot” drawing on the memoir “The Silent Escape” by the late Romanian political prisoner Lena Constante, to productions titled “Locked Within Myself” and “The Sweetness of Doing Nothing LTD.”
Patricia Prisacariu, director of “Waiting for Godot,” said it was a sometimes difficult but memorable and worthy experience.

item.title: Heavy fighting erupts in Haiti as armed forces fight gangs to regain control of key corridor
item.description:
Heavy fighting erupts in Haiti as armed forces fight gangs to regain control of key corridor
Armed forces in Haiti have launched an aggressive operation to remove powerful gangs long entrenched in a key corridor that connects the country’s capital to its western and southern regionsByDÁNICA COTO Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 12:47 PM
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico -- Armed forces in Haiti launched an aggressive operation on Thursday to remove powerful gangs long entrenched in a key corridor that connects the country’s capital to its western and southern regions.
It is the first significant operation in the five years since violent gangs seized control of Martissant, located in the western tip of Port-au-Prince.
Haiti’s National Police posted a video on X stating that at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in Martissant during a fight with police officers working with a task force composed of members from Vectus Global, a private security firm founded by former U.S. Navy SEAL and Blackwater founder Erik Prince.
Local media reported heavy gunfire and explosive drones in the area as Haiti’s police posted a video of armored vehicles rumbling through the community.
Martissant is located along Route 2, the main road that leads out of Port-au-Prince to important western and southern cities. Thousands of people would travel through Martissant every day before gangs seized control of the area more than five years ago, disrupting the country’s economy as they prevented goods from entering or leaving the capital. Gangs have since charged tolls or randomly opened fire on cars or buses that dare cross through.
Ever since gangs seized absolute control of Martissant, aid workers and Haitian civilians have been forced to take alternative transportation or use rural back roads.

item.title: Wife of Italian fugitive convicted of terrorism arrested in Argentina over his escape
item.description:
Wife of Italian fugitive convicted of terrorism arrested in Argentina over his escape
Argentine authorities have arrested the wife of an Italian fugitive convicted of terrorism-related crimesByALMUDENA CALATRAVA Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 12:36 PM
Share
BUENOS AIRES, Argentina -- Argentine authorities have arrested the wife of an Italian fugitive convicted of terrorism-related crimes on suspicion of helping him escape house arrest by rappelling from a fifth-floor apartment in Buenos Aires last week.
Betina Erika Köpcke, 77, remained in custody Thursday after being arrested in the same neighborhood where her husband, Leonardo Bertulazzi, 74, had been confined, Security Minister Alejandra Monteoliva said.
Bertulazzi, a former member of Italy’s left-wing Red Brigades militant group, was awaiting extradition to serve a 27-year prison sentence for aggravated kidnapping and possession of explosives, among other crimes. The group was responsible for kidnappings and killings of judges, police officers, business executives and politicians in Italy during the 1970s and 1980s.
On Nov. 10, Bertulazzi used ropes and a harness to descend from his fifth-floor apartment to a neighboring house before reaching a vacant lot. Security camera footage showed him climbing over a gate and jumping onto the street.
Monteoliva said evidence recovered from a cellphone Bertulazzi left behind suggested his wife helped plan the escape. The phone contained photographs taken in October 2025 showing Köpcke near the gate through which he fled, the Security Ministry said.
Argentina’s Security Ministry offered a reward of 20 million pesos (about $12,000) for information leading to Bertulazzi’s capture.
Authorities did not immediately detect the escape because Bertulazzi had tampered with his electronic ankle monitor.

item.title: Newborn dies after suspected female genital mutilation in Senegal; relatives arrested
item.description:
Newborn dies after suspected female genital mutilation in Senegal; relatives arrested
Three people have been arrested in eastern Senegal after a newborn baby girl died following alleged female genital mutilationByBABACAR DIONE Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 11:16 AM
DAKAR, Senegal -- Three people, including the father and grandmother of a newborn baby girl who bled to death after allegedly undergoing female genital mutilation in eastern Senegal, have been arrested, a local official said Thursday.
The baby was allegedly subjected to the procedure on Nov. 12, just a day after she was born in the eastern Tambacounda region, Ndiaye Bousso, the regional director of family affairs, told The Associated Press.
The father was arrested Wednesday on suspicion of arranging the procedure, Bousso said. His mother and another woman suspected of carrying it out had been detained days earlier.
According to Bousso, the baby's paternal grandmother offered to bathe the newborn with the help of the other woman, but allegedly performed the mutilation without the mother’s knowledge. The mother later discovered that her daughter was in pain and bleeding.
The baby haemorrhaged severely and was referred to a regional hospital in Tambacounda on Friday, but died on the way, Bousso said.
Female genital mutilation, or FGM, has been illegal in Senegal since 1999 and is punishable by up to five years in prison, or life imprisonment if the procedure results in death.
Around 20% of women and girls ages 15-49 in Senegal are believed to have undergone FGM, according to the latest data from UNICEF. Its supporters claim the practice is rooted in traditions, but authorities have stepped up awareness campaigns in recent years to discourage it.

item.title: Myanmar is the first state found responsible for genocide. How did the UN court rule in other cases?
item.description:
Myanmar is the first state found responsible for genocide. How did the UN court rule in other cases?
The United Nations’ top court has for the first time ruled that a nation committed what legal scholars call the crime of crimes, finding that Myanmar committed genocide in a brutal 2017 military crackdown against the Rohingya minorityByMIKE CORDER Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 11:14 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
THE HAGUE, Netherlands -- The United Nations' top court has for the first time ruled that a nation committed what legal scholars call the crime of crimes, finding that Myanmar committed genocide in a brutal 2017 military crackdown against the Rohingya minority.
The International Court of Justice has been asked to reach that conclusion before, but never found enough evidence to make the determination of a state-sponsored genocide like the one targeting the Rohingya.
The World Court has more cases on its docket dealing with alleged breaches of the 1948 Genocide Convention, including a politically charged case about Israel’s actions in Gaza.
What happened: The Srebrenica massacre was a peak in the violence of Bosnia’s 1992-95 war, which came after the breakup of Yugoslavia unleashed nationalist passions and territorial ambitions across the region.
On July 11, 1995, Serbs overran Srebrenica, at the time a U.N.-protected safe area. They separated at least 8,000 Bosniak men and boys from their wives, mothers and sisters and slaughtered them. Those who tried to escape were chased through the woods and over the mountains around town.
How the court ruled: The court, basing itself in part on verdicts at a United Nations war crimes tribunal, said in a 2007 ruling that the Srebrenica killings amounted to genocide. However, it did not find Serbia responsible. It did find Serbia had violated its obligation to prevent genocide. That obligation is enshrined in the 1948 Genocide Convention.

item.title: 4 men found guilty of sex crimes against British woman in a case that recalls Gisèle Pelicot's
item.description:
4 men found guilty of sex crimes against British woman in a case that recalls Gisèle Pelicot's
Four British men have been found guilty of multiple sexual crimes against a woman whose ex-husband drugged and advertised her for sex onlineByPAN PYLAS Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 11:02 AM
LONDON -- Four British men were found guilty Thursday of multiple sexual crimes, including rape, against a woman whose then-husband drugged and advertised her for sex online, in a case that raised widespread comparisons to that of Gisèle Pelicot in France.
Joanne Young, who waived her right to anonymity as Pelicot had, spoke of her “relief” at the jury verdict and urged other women who have experienced anything similar to go to authorities in the knowledge that they “can be believed and understood.”
“Knowing what has happened to me without my knowledge or consent has been incredibly difficult to process, and this abuse has cost me my life as I knew it,” she said outside Winchester Crown Court in southern England. “The person I trusted most in the world betrayed me in the most horrific way."
The 49-year-old mother of three spoke after the jury found the four men, whose ages range from 32 to 62, guilty of abusing her at her home in Swindon after being recruited on the internet.
Her ex-husband, Philip Young, had previously pleaded guilty to dozens of offenses including 11 counts of rape and 11 of administering a substance with intent.
Norman Macksoni, 48, was found guilty of one charge of rape. Richard Wilkins, 62, was found guilty of one count of rape and one of assault by penetration. Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, was convicted of sexual assault by penetration and sexual touching while Mohammed Hassan was found guilty of one count of sexual touching.
A sixth defendant, Dean Hamilton, 47, admitted one charge of assault by penetration, two of sexual assault and one of rape.
